title: Profile controlled-3: the compose db service stops carrying POSTGRES_PASSWORD in Config.Env
description:
LEAF spun out of task-9255156954724b7dbbcbf03ae2aaa11c (the compose-managed incumbent leaks every variable value through docker inspect) by architect-ed42e60a, 2026-09-09, after the owner chose the real fix over a documented carve-out. That row is the CONSUMER and names this row in its dependsOn. Split because the db service lives in the PROFILE-GOLDENED base compose file and changing its bytes is a profile version bump with a control-room mirror, which is a different and larger job than the app-side override the consumer owns.

THE LEAK. `controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:239-243` emits the base `docker-compose.yml` db service with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` under `environment:`, so the password sits in that container's `.Config.Env` and `docker inspect` prints it to anyone who can reach the docker socket. Measured on the parent epic: a value passed through compose `environment:` gives 1 grep hit in inspect output; the same value delivered as a mounted file gives 0.

THE SHAPE, and it needs ONE measurement before it is pinned. Use a compose SECRET sourced from the compose environment, plus the postgres image's own documented `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE`:

    services:
      db:
        environment:
          POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-app}
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/postgres_password
          POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-app}
        secrets:
          - postgres_password
    secrets:
      postgres_password:
        environment: POSTGRES_PASSWORD

`POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE` is a PATH, so it is safe in Config.Env; the value reaches the container only as file content. The operator flow is unchanged - the value still comes from `.env`, which is already gitignored. MEASURE FIRST: `secrets.environment` needs a recent Compose (v2.23+ in the spec). The Docker daemon was DOWN on this host at filing time, so confirm the running Compose version supports it before pinning the golden. If it does not, the fallback is a `file:`-sourced secret, but that changes what an operator must set up and must be disclosed rather than slipped in.

DO NOT LOSE THE FAIL-FAST. Today `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` makes compose refuse with a readable message when the variable is unset. `secrets.environment` takes no `:?` form, so an unset variable would silently mount an EMPTY password. Keep an equivalent fail-fast - a top-level `x-` extension field carrying the `:?` reference is one way, postgres refusing an empty password file is another - and prove it with an arm rather than assuming it.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a:
- `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:22-24` states the rule this row obeys: "A tree change is a profile VERSION BUMP plus a lockfile re-mint, not a re-bake of the numbers below (task rail 4)." Do not re-bake `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` hashes to make an arm green without bumping.
- `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` at :32-56 pins `docker-compose.yml  288945fa1cb9987f9bd53988e947bbdb4b46007a59a86237f6efdb229f718a1b`, and `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT = 23` is pinned independently so a dropped file cannot shrink both sides.
- `EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE` at :91 is a byte-exact array asserted with `toEqual` at :192; the db environment lines are at :102.
- The literal `"controlled-2"` appears in FOUR places: `controlled-profile-generator.ts:26` (the source), `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:163`, and - HAND-TRANSCRIBED, per its own comment at `live-new-product.tsx:38-45` - `apps/control-room/src/v2/products/live-new-product.tsx:49` and `live-new-product.test.tsx:52`. All four move together.
- `assets/` holds `controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` and `controlled-profile-v2-lock.yaml`, one per version, so a v3 needs its own. This change touches no dependency, so the v3 lock is expected to be byte-identical to v2 - say so in the record rather than leaving a silent copy.
- `controlled-profile-migrate.test.ts` starts postgres with a direct `docker run --env`, NOT through compose, so it does not consume this service and must not be edited.
definitionOfDone: The generated base docker-compose.yml delivers the postgres password as a compose SECRET rather than through `environment:`, and no emitted byte of any generated file carries a credential literal - the existing cross-directory CHANGE_ME read-back arm still passes unchanged.

A running db container started from the generated compose shows NO password value in `docker inspect` (grep count 0 for a planted value), while still authenticating - prove it by connecting, not by reading the compose file. If the running Compose version does not support an environment-sourced secret, say so with the measured version and take the disclosed file-sourced fallback.

An unset POSTGRES_PASSWORD still fails fast with a readable message. An arm proves it: today `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` does this and `secrets.environment` takes no `:?` form, so an empty-password silent start is the regression this clause exists to catch.

CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION is bumped to controlled-3 in all FOUR places that carry the literal, including the two hand-transcribed control-room mirrors, and assets/controlled-profile-v3-lock.yaml exists. GOLDEN_MANIFEST and EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE are updated as a consequence of the bump, never re-baked to silence a red.
GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT still matches the emitted file count, and it is updated only if this row actually adds or removes a file.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test AND pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test both EXIT 0 with their count lines quoted. The control-room leg is mandatory and not optional: the two version mirrors live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg (epic rail 1).

implementationPlan.description: PRE-FLIGHT, and one measurement decides the whole shape. Read comment-8751c58226b74ea09cfbad9a5b201b87 FIRST — it amends DoD item 4 (no v3 lockfile asset is minted) and is authoritative where it conflicts with the field. Then: (1) bring Docker up and record `docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'` AND `docker compose version` — the daemon was DOWN on this host at filing time, so nothing docker-backed is measured until you see those. (2) DECIDE THE SECRET SOURCE by measurement, not by reading a spec table. Write a throwaway compose file in the scratchpad using `secrets: { postgres_password: { environment: POSTGRES_PASSWORD } }` and run `docker compose config` against it. If the running Compose resolves it, take the environment-sourced form: the value keeps coming from `.env` and the operator's setup flow is unchanged. If it errors, take the `file:`-sourced fallback, and DISCLOSE in the completion record that it changes what an operator must create by hand — do not ship that quietly. Tear the throwaway down. (3) Re-measure the anchors this plan names: `DOCKER_COMPOSE` in controlled-profile-root-templates.ts around :232-256, `EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE` at controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:91 asserted by `toEqual` at :192, the `docker-compose.yml` line in `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` at :37, `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT = 23` at :30, the version arm at :163, and `LOCKFILE_ASSET` at controlled-profile-generator.ts:118.

Change the db service in the base compose, in controlled-profile-root-templates.ts `DOCKER_COMPOSE`. Replace the `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}` line under `environment:` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/postgres_password` — a PATH, which is safe to carry in `.Config.Env` — add a service-level `secrets: [postgres_password]` list, and add a top-level `secrets:` block whose source is whichever form step 1 measured. `POSTGRES_USER` and `POSTGRES_DB` stay as they are: a username and a database name are not credentials, and narrowing them would move the golden for no security gain. The healthcheck's `pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-app} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-app}` is unaffected and must not be touched. PRESERVE THE FAIL-FAST, WHICH IS THE EASIEST THING TO LOSE HERE. Today `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` makes `docker compose up` refuse with a readable message when the variable is unset. An environment-sourced secret takes no `:?` form, so an unset variable would mount an EMPTY password file and postgres would start with trust-like behaviour or fail obscurely on first connect. Keep an equivalent — a top-level `x-` extension field carrying the `:?` reference is one way that compose still interpolates and errors on — and measure which failure the operator actually sees rather than assuming postgres refuses. Update the file's own header comment: "Every credential is read from the environment" is about to be half true, and the comment is what the next reader trusts.

Bump the profile version on the daemon side. `controlled-profile-generator.ts:26` goes to `controlled-3`, and `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:163` ("identifies the migration-capable profile with a new version") follows. DO NOT MINT A v3 LOCKFILE ASSET and do not repoint `LOCKFILE_ASSET` at :118: it is a hard-coded literal with no coupling to the version, this row moves no dependency, and `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`'s `pnpm-lock.yaml 0963d16c...` hash MUST NOT move — if it does, something changed that this row did not intend, and that is a stop-and-investigate signal rather than a number to re-bake. Add a short comment at `LOCKFILE_ASSET` recording that controlled-3 deliberately ships controlled-2's lockfile because no dependency moved, so the next version bump does not read the stale `v2` filename as an oversight. The governing rule is stated at controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:22-24 — a tree change is a version bump plus a lockfile re-mint, never a re-bake of the golden numbers — and a re-mint that yields identical bytes satisfies it.

Move the two HAND-TRANSCRIBED control-room mirrors, which are the half most likely to be forgotten. `apps/control-room/src/v2/products/live-new-product.tsx:49` carries `export const CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION = "controlled-2"` and `live-new-product.test.tsx:52` pins that literal. Its own comment at :38-45 explains why it is transcribed rather than imported — apps/control-room cannot import apps/daemon (no workspace edge, no tsconfig `paths`, a deep relative import is TS6059) and the daemon discloses the string on no browser-readable route — and it instructs the reader to re-check it whenever the generator moves. Update the transcription, the pinned literal, and the comment's history line, which currently records only `controlled-1 -> controlled-2 on 2026-09-06`. EPIC RAIL 1 MAKES THIS LOAD-BEARING: these two files live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg, so a missed bump ships silently and surfaces later as `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN @ DAEMON_INGRESS` in the operator's form. It fails closed, but it fails in production rather than in the suite.

Update the goldens as a CONSEQUENCE of steps 2 and 3, never to silence a red. `EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE` (controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:91, `toEqual` at :192) moves line for line and stays an exact `toEqual` — do not loosen it to `toContain`. The `docker-compose.yml` entry in `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` at :37 takes its new sha256; every OTHER manifest line, `pnpm-lock.yaml` included, must be byte-unchanged, and `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT = 23` stays 23 because this row adds and removes no file. Add arms that pin the new BEHAVIOUR rather than only the new bytes, since a byte golden agrees with whatever it was last set to: the emitted compose carries no `POSTGRES_PASSWORD:` assignment under any service's `environment:`, it does carry `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE` pointing at a path under `/run/secrets/`, and the existing cross-directory `CHANGE_ME` read-back arm proving no emitted file carries a credential literal still passes UNCHANGED. THEN VERIFY THE OTHER GENERATOR'S PARSER rather than trusting my measurement of it: `deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:180-196` `composeServices` decides service membership by column-0 lines, so a top-level `secrets:` block should turn collection off and be skipped, leaving the merge arm at :306-313 asserting `{app, db, proxy}` intact. Run that file and confirm. If a `secrets` key registers as a fourth service, fix the parser there and say so — that file is in this row's roster for exactly this check.

LIVE PROOF — DoD items 2 and 3, and neither may be discharged by reading the generated file. Materialize the scaffold into a scratch directory, write a `.env` whose POSTGRES_PASSWORD is a planted non-credential-shaped canary value, and `docker compose up` the db service. Then: (a) `docker inspect <db container>` and grep for the planted value — the count must be 0, and quote the command and the count, not a summary of it. Sweep more than `.Config.Env`: check `.Config.Cmd`, `.Config.Entrypoint`, `.Config.Labels` (compose writes a config-hash label on every container it manages) and the output of `docker compose config`, which resolves and prints interpolated values. (b) Prove it still AUTHENTICATES — connect with that password and run a trivial query, the way the platform canary does with `PGPASSWORD`. A container that starts is not a container that accepted the password. (c) DoD 3's fail-fast arm: with POSTGRES_PASSWORD unset, `docker compose up` must refuse with a readable message naming the variable. Quote the actual stderr. An empty-password silent start is the regression this clause exists to catch, and it passes every byte-golden arm in step 5. NON-VACUITY: run (a) once against the PRE-CHANGE templates and confirm the grep count is 1, so the zero afterwards means something. TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH INCLUDING THE FAILURE ONES — `docker compose down --volumes`, then a `docker ps -a` census proving nothing of yours survived. This scaffold publishes host port 5432, so it cannot run beside the platform e2e files; hold `full-suite-gate` for the duration and announce GATE START and GATE END. Epic rail 4 makes a leaked container or held port inadmissible for every later gate on this board.

VERIFICATION and adversarial review — DoD item 6. Run each leg standalone in the FOREGROUND, no pipes and no `;` chains, since a piped run reports tail's exit code. Legs: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. THE CONTROL-ROOM LEGS ARE MANDATORY, not a courtesy: the two version mirrors from step 4 live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg (epic rail 1), so without them a missed bump ships green. Quote each command, exit code and `Test Files N passed` count line — an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED, and `pnpm --filter` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 on a bad package name. Apply the path-attributed baseline for any repo-wide red: failing paths at the merge-base versus HEAD, delta intersected with this row's six owned paths must be EMPTY, foreign red quoted verbatim. THEN READ THE DIFF AS AN ATTACKER. Questions this change earns: can the password reach a log line when postgres fails to read the secret file? Does `docker compose config` or the compose config-hash label expose it? What happens with a password containing a newline, a `$`, or a trailing space — does the secret file round-trip it byte for byte, and does `pg_isready` still pass? Is the fail-fast arm falsifiable — remove the guard, confirm the arm goes RED, restore. RESTORE PROOF: back the mutated template out of tree to `%TEMP%/moe-task-7693a195c0-<basename>-<workerId>`, the task id in the path is mandatory because seat ids are reused across relaunches and a seat-keyed backup has held a stale vintage on this host; hash the LIVE file at window-open and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore, with no full-suite lease held. Put the gate table in a task COMMENT first — completionSummary truncates silently at 2000 chars mid-word — then report every touched path in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT AMENDMENT TO MY OWN DoD ITEM 4 — THE v3 LOCKFILE ASSET IS NOT REQUIRED. architect-ed42e60a, 2026-09-09, planning this row. I wrote item 4 before measuring how the lockfile asset is selected; this comment corrects it and is authoritative where it conflicts with the field.

WHAT I ASSUMED: that `assets/` is keyed by profile version (it holds `controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` and `controlled-profile-v2-lock.yaml`), so controlled-3 needs `controlled-profile-v3-lock.yaml`.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured at `controlled-profile-generator.ts:118`:

    const LOCKFILE_ASSET = new URL("./assets/controlled-profile-v2-lock.yaml", import.meta.url);

The asset path is a HARD-CODED LITERAL, not derived from `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION`. Nothing couples the filename to the version, and no arm asserts the coupling — `git grep 'v2-lock\|v1-lock\|LOCKFILE_ASSET'` returns only that line and the `readFileSync` on the next.

WHY THAT CHANGES THE ANSWER. This row moves no dependency: it edits a compose service's environment block. So the emitted `pnpm-lock.yaml` bytes are IDENTICAL, and `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`'s `pnpm-lock.yaml 0963d16c8e4227942c882ed08bdba2f8a7e74d4339b92bc6e10952357c286265` must NOT move. Minting `controlled-profile-v3-lock.yaml` would add a thousands-of-lines byte-identical duplicate to the repo for zero content change — and the generator's own comment at :107-108 says the asset exists precisely BECAUSE it is too large to inline.

DoD ITEM 4 IS THEREFORE AMENDED TO: "CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION is bumped to controlled-3 in all FOUR places that carry the literal, including the two hand-transcribed control-room mirrors. NO new lockfile asset is minted: this row moves no dependency, so controlled-3 ships controlled-2's lockfile bytes and GOLDEN_MANIFEST's pnpm-lock.yaml hash MUST NOT move — a moved lock hash is evidence something unintended changed. Record in the completion summary that the asset was deliberately not duplicated and why. GOLDEN_MANIFEST's docker-compose.yml hash and EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE are updated as a consequence of the bump, never re-baked to silence a red."

The rest of the DoD stands as filed. Note that `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:22-24` states the governing rule — "A tree change is a profile VERSION BUMP plus a lockfile re-mint, not a re-bake of the numbers below (task rail 4)" — and a re-mint that produces identical bytes IS satisfied by shipping the same asset. What that rule forbids is editing the hashes without bumping the version, which this row does not do.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, so the worker does not re-derive it. Adding a top-level `secrets:` block to the base compose does NOT break `composeServices` in `deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:180-196`: that parser sets `inServices = line.startsWith("services:")` on any column-0 line, so a top-level `secrets:` correctly turns collection off and its children are skipped. A service-level `secrets:` list is indented four and is collected into the db body as any other key. The merge arm at :306-313 asserting `{app, db, proxy}` therefore still holds. VERIFY THIS RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT — that file is in this row's path roster for the check, and it is the one place a base-compose shape change could silently register as a fourth service.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: MECHANISM: a compose SECRET sourced from the compose ENVIRONMENT plus the postgres image's own documented `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE`. Chosen over a `file:`-sourced secret because the value already lives in `.env` and compose can read it from there, so the operator's setup flow does not change; the file-sourced form makes every operator hand-create a secret file before `docker compose up` works, which is a UX regression shipped under a security fix. It stays the DISCLOSED fallback if the running Compose is too old to resolve an environment-sourced secret, and step 1 measures that rather than trusting a spec version table — the Docker daemon was down at planning time. Rejected: leaving the password in `environment:` and having the app read it — that is the bug. Rejected: docker swarm-style external secrets — needs a swarm, which the scaffold does not assume. THE LOCKFILE QUESTION was resolved against my own first draft of the DoD and the correction is in comment-8751c58226b74ea09cfbad9a5b201b87: `LOCKFILE_ASSET` at controlled-profile-generator.ts:118 is a HARD-CODED literal naming the v2 asset, with no coupling to `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` and no arm asserting one, so a version bump does not by itself require a new asset. This row moves no dependency, so minting `controlled-profile-v3-lock.yaml` would add a thousands-of-lines byte-identical duplicate for zero content change. controlled-3 ships controlled-2's lockfile and the manifest's lock hash must not move. SCOPE: the APP service's DATABASE_URL is deliberately NOT in this row. It lives in `docker-compose.override.yml`, generated by a different generator that is not profile-goldened, and it belongs to the consumer task-9255156954724b7dbbcbf03ae2aaa11c. Fixing both here would have meant one row spanning two generators and two golden families.

Every byte-golden arm in step 5 passes through that regression without noticing, which is exactly why DoD 3 demands an arm and why step 6 demands the actual stderr be quoted.
